oil.summary: Crude markets delivered a split session Friday: WTI surged 3.52% to $103.00/bbl while Brent dipped 1.47% to $111.51, widening the spread sharply. The divergence reflects a volatile week shaped by Middle East escalation — Iran has explicitly targeted Saudi refineries and infrastructure, drawing Egypt into a defensive posture and pushing Brent toward a five-month high. A headline citing '$120 oil is almost here' captured the geopolitical bid, yet physical Middle East crude prices softened even as futures rallied, suggesting paper markets are running ahead of spot fundamentals. Refined products cracked lower: RBOB fell 1.54% and heating oil dropped 3.22%, hinting at demand-side concerns. On the supply side, a US partner in Venezuela lifted output ~20,000 b/d, while the first Russian diesel cargo bound for New York departed Primorsk. A CFTC probe into a two-minute 6-million-barrel futures dump adds a market-integrity overhang. Options markets price a 77% probability of an OPEC cut at the next meeting.
drivers: Middle East escalation — Iran targeting Saudi energy infrastructure and Egypt entering the conflict — sustaining a geopolitical risk premium in WTI and Brent futures
Refined product weakness (RBOB -1.54%, heating oil -3.22%) diverging from crude strength, suggesting demand concerns or crack-spread compression
Supply offsets from Venezuela production gains (~20,000 b/d) and first Russian diesel cargo to the US, while physical Middle East crude softens versus paper benchmarks

gas.summary: Natural gas markets split sharply along geographic lines Friday. Henry Hub spiked 8.98% intraday to $3.048/MMBtu, a notable single-session jump even as the monthly trend remains down 7.58%, pointing to weather or near-term supply tightness rather than a structural re-rating. In Europe, TTF surged another 3.62% to 93.3 €/MWh — its highest level since 2022 — driven by Middle East escalation restricting Qatari LNG flows. TTF is now up 24.22% over the past month, a significant supply-shock move. Domestically, the US rig count held flat for a second consecutive week despite elevated oil prices, signaling producers are not yet responding to price signals with incremental drilling. Australia's gas-fired generation hit a quarter-century low in Q3 as renewables and grid-scale batteries displaced gas, a structural demand-erosion signal for that market.
drivers: TTF at highest since 2022, up 24% in a month, as Middle East conflict curtails Qatari LNG flows into Europe
Henry Hub +8.98% on the day despite a soft monthly trend, suggesting acute near-term tightness rather than a structural shift
US rig count unchanged for a second week, indicating supply response to higher prices remains absent

power.summary: The power and carbon complex offers a mixed picture today. EU carbon (EUA) is essentially flat on the day at $82.27/EUA (+0.02%), with the one-month performance near-zero (-0.23%), suggesting the ETS market has not yet repriced the energy shock fully. The dominant cross-sector story remains surging TTF gas (+3.62% today, +24% over one month), which mechanically pressures gas-fired generation economics and should support EUA demand — though the carbon price is not yet moving in tandem. Australia illustrates the secular displacement trend: gas-fired power hit a 25-year quarterly low as renewables and battery storage set records, reducing that market's gas-burn and carbon intensity. Ukraine's mass drone strike on a Russian oil terminal in St. Petersburg adds a further geopolitical layer to European energy security. Headline flow for this sector is thinner than oil; carbon price action remains subdued relative to the underlying energy price stress.
drivers: TTF +24% over one month pressures European gas-fired generation margins, yet EUA carbon price remains flat, suggesting a lagged or decoupled market response
Australia's gas power generation at a 25-year Q3 low as record renewables and grid-scale batteries displace thermal dispatch
Ukraine drone strike on St. Petersburg oil terminal adds European energy-security risk, reinforcing the case for fuel-switching and carbon market volatility ahead
